title: Free-choice album for Norman Granz
summary: Granz gave Carter carte blanche for Pablo albums, and he is still deciding what to do.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Well, let me maybe go at it like this. I don't know if you've been asked this question before, but you've done a lot of music for hire, in effect; that is, for lack of a more precise term, I'll call it commercial music; that is, music for film, for television,

etc. -- or arrangements for other bands, for which there are certain musical specifications. And I'm not sure if this question is gonna make much sense, but if you were gonna do something strictly for yourself and not have any kind of constraints; I mean, that is, you could use all the different kinds of instruments as you wanted, as many musicians or as few musicians as you liked, no time restraints, no financial restraints -- what would you do, or is this, maybe a silly question?

It is not a silly question. It's a very good question, Jim. It's a very good question particularly at this moment. Because I've just been talking about my next album or two that I'm going to do for Norman Granz for Pablo. And Norman has given me carte blanche do do anything I want to do. Now when I say "Anything" I want to do," you know, go and write or hire as many musicians as you want to, and this is probably for one or two albums.

Now the difficulty here with me is that it's a matter of making a decision. What do I want to do, you know? And you always feel like, gee, if I could only do just that what you really wanted to do, how would you go about it, what would you do? Of course, I'm doing one album coming up that I'm going to be doing with Ray Bryant -- it's just a quartet album, but then following that, I'll be doing an album with a big band, a number of men of my choice, the type of music of my choice, the composition of my choice -- my own or something else, you know.
And it's not like I had unlimited funds at my disposal and I wanted to go and do something for myself at my own financial risk, and I might then say see, well, gee, I might make 6 albums.
Then, you know, I wouldn't have to worry so much about what am I going to do with this one album.

You know, I could do a series of different things, but I know that at least I can do one album now with no restrictions; no limitations, which of course, I don't intend to abuse -- I don't want to do anything on an ego trip and say, well, gee, you know, I can do anything I want -- let's go out and get 100 men, or, you know, hire the L.A. Symphony, and ... something like that.
But I'm not sure what I'm going to do. I'm really doing a lot of thinking about it at this moment.
